main-usb-port.whyExists: It supplies power and carries commands and results between the computer and the Proxmark3.
main-usb-port.missingImpact: Electron could not detect or communicate with the board through the PM3 client.

side-usb-port.whyExists: This connector belongs to the physical board design, but its exact role must be confirmed for this specific board revision.
side-usb-port.missingImpact: No impact should be claimed until the connector role and board revision are verified.
firmwareModules: Unknown until the connector role is verified

hf-antenna.whyExists: It creates and receives the 13.56 MHz radio field used by HF and NFC tags.
hf-antenna.missingImpact: HF cards could not be powered, detected or read by this board.

lf-antenna-module.whyExists: It creates and receives the low-frequency field used by 125 kHz and compatible LF tags.
lf-antenna-module.missingImpact: LF credentials and transponders could not be detected by the board.

xilinx-spartan-fpga.whyExists: It performs radio timing and signal-processing work that must happen much faster and more precisely than normal application code.
xilinx-spartan-fpga.missingImpact: Most HF and LF radio operations would no longer work.

atmel-mcu.whyExists: It runs the main firmware, communicates over USB and coordinates commands, memory and the FPGA.
atmel-mcu.missingImpact: The board could not boot its main firmware or respond to Electron.

flash-memory.whyExists: It stores data or firmware-related content that must remain available after power is removed.
flash-memory.missingImpact: Features that depend on persistent storage or external flash would be unavailable.

buffer-chips.whyExists: They buffer and isolate digital signal lines so connected board sections receive clean, correctly driven signals.
buffer-chips.missingImpact: Signal paths could become unreliable or stop working even though Electron cannot address these chips directly.
firmwareModules: No direct module; used indirectly by timed FPGA and MCU signals

button.whyExists: It gives the firmware a physical input for guided or standalone actions.
button.missingImpact: Physical confirmation and button-driven standalone workflows would be unavailable.

power-section.whyExists: It converts and stabilises USB power for the MCU, FPGA and radio electronics.
power-section.missingImpact: The board would be unstable, fail to start or risk hardware damage.
firmwareModules: No direct software module; monitored indirectly

power-led.whyExists: It gives immediate visual confirmation that the board is receiving power.
power-led.missingImpact: The board could still work, but users would lose a useful power indicator.
firmwareModules: Normally hardware-driven, not a firmware capability

led-a.whyExists: It provides visible firmware feedback during operations.
led-a.missingImpact: The operation may still work, but visual feedback would be reduced.

led-b.whyExists: It provides visible firmware feedback during operations.
led-b.missingImpact: The operation may still work, but visual feedback would be reduced.

led-c.missingImpact: The operation may still work, but visual feedback would be reduced.
